items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: Bix, later on with Goldkett, showed that he knew some of this thing.

ctx.x: On the beat? Ahead the beat?

It's ahead. Da, Those notes aren't always in it. But I mean, the essence of it is in it. You can feel it in the Pollock Band. And see, Bix had slid through Chicago so fast, really, and had spent so much time with Hoagie and the Poet Monk House in Bloomington, Indiana, and in playing around in there, that he developed this lovely singing style that he developed, but with this underlying softer beat than the Chicagoans later developed. Bix would have been perfectly wonderful in that kind of a Chicago band. But Bix,…
Would you call the loudness a feature of dynamics, or just they played loud all the time?
